author: Rizzinomics
quote:
After 13 years of waiting, apparently Rockstar decided what the world really needed wasn't another Grand Theft Auto game, but a masterclass in being the perfect boyfriend. 

Welcome to Grand Theft Auto VI, where apparently being a criminal mastermind takes a backseat to buying your girlfriend flowers, picking up groceries, fixing the house, buying her clothes and making sure she's happy. Jason Duval isn't a criminal protagonist. He's a glorified personal assistant with a criminal record. The problem isn't that GTA has romance or relationships. 

Previous games had relationships, family drama and domestic storylines. The problem is the apparent emphasis on making Jason's relationship with Lucia such a central part of the experience, with an increasingly one-sided dynamic that makes him feel more like her errand boy than an independent character. Remember when GTA was about freedom? Robbing banks, causing absolute mayhem, making questionable decisions and being a complete menace to society? Now we're apparently being taught how to maintain a healthy household. 

And the irony is that Rockstar has spent years building a reputation around giving players freedom, only to introduce a protagonist whose personality seems to revolve around keeping his girlfriend satisfied. There's nothing wrong with having a relationship in a video game. There's something wrong with making relationship maintenance feel like a substitute for the criminal escapism people came to GTA for. 

13 years of anticipation for Grand Theft Auto, only to get Grand Theft Boyfriend. What a disappointment in terms of creative direction.
